answer:
DDP replicates parameters and optimizer state, divides examples across workers, and synchronizes gradients. ZeRO-1 shards optimizer states; ZeRO-2 additionally shards gradients; ZeRO-3/FSDP additionally shards parameters, gathering needed parameters around computation. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.02054)

Tensor parallelism splits individual matrix operations, requiring collectives within layers. Pipeline parallelism assigns different layers to stages and sends activations/gradients between them; microbatches reduce bubbles. Sequence parallelism distributes selected activation operations across tokens, whereas context parallelism distributes long sequences and exchanges information needed for attention. Terminology varies by implementation. [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.08053) [3](https://jax-ml.github.io/scaling-book/)

Choose according to the constrained resource: model-state capacity, activation memory, per-layer compute, or global throughput. Combinations are common. A theoretical memory saving may be erased by slow collectives, temporary all-gathers, poor overlap, or small microbatches; profile the whole step.
